title: Coherence of normalized cohomology and complete truncation triangles in t-exact systems
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset [def-weil-size-convention]. For each $i\in I$ let $\mathcal C_i$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with a bounded t-structure [def-weil-t-structure]. For $i\le j$ let $T_{j/i}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ be an exact functor with its specified shift comparison, preserving both halves in every degree. Assume $T_{i/i}=1$ and exact natural associators $a_{k,j,i}:T_{k/j}T_{j/i}\cong T_{k/i}$ satisfying the unit and pentagon equations and commuting with shifts. Write $c^-_{j/i,r}:T_{j/i}\tau_i^{\le r}\cong\tau_j^{\le r}T_{j/i}$ and $c^+_{j/i,r}:T_{j/i}\tau_i^{\ge r}\cong\tau_j^{\ge r}T_{j/i}$ for the normalized comparisons of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison], characterized by $\iota c^-=T(\iota)$ and $c^+T(\pi)=\pi$. Put $H_i^r(K)=(\tau_i^{\ge r}\tau_i^{\le r}K)[r]$, viewed as an object in the heart [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles].

For either truncation $\tau$, the comparisons obey
$$c_{k/i,r,K}\,a_{k,j,i,\tau K}=\tau_k(a_{k,j,i,K})\,c_{k/j,r,T_{j/i}K}\,T_{k/j}(c_{j/i,r,K}),$$
and $c_{i/i,r}=1$. For each $T=T_{j/i}$ the triple $(c^-_{j/i,r,K},1_{TK},c^+_{j/i,r+1,K})$ is a natural isomorphism from the image under $T$ of the entire distinguished truncation triangle of $K$ to the truncation triangle of $TK$. Its third square is explicitly
$$\delta_{TK}c^+_{j/i,r+1,K}=(c^-_{j/i,r,K})[1]\,\sigma_{T,\tau_i^{\le r}K}\,T(\delta_K),$$
where $\delta$ is the truncation boundary and $\sigma_T:T(-[1])\cong(T-)[1]$ is the specified shift comparison. These isomorphisms commute with canonical changes of cutoff and obey the same identity and composition equations as $c$.

Composing the two normalized truncation comparisons with the iterated shift comparison gives natural isomorphisms $h^r_{j/i}:T_{j/i}H_i^r\cong H_j^rT_{j/i}$, with $h^r_{i/i}=1$ and
$$h^r_{k/i,K}\,a_{k,j,i,H_i^rK}=H_k^r(a_{k,j,i,K})\,h^r_{k/j,T_{j/i}K}\,T_{k/j}(h^r_{j/i,K}).$$
All assertions also hold for a single exact t-exact functor and are compatible with exact natural transformations between such functors. Here all triangle comparisons are comparisons in the triangulated categories, and $H^r$ is the degree-zero object, not an unshifted degree-$r$ complex.

proof.text: For a system associator a, apply the composition clause of texact_truncation_comparison to the actual normalized comparisons for T_ij followed by T_jk. Apply its transformation clause to a and substitute those composition formulas, obtaining both system truncation equations. Applying the transformation clause to eqToIso(unit) and then its identity clause gives the diagonal truncation equations.

proof.text: The diagonal equality of underlying functors does not by itself identify their shift structures. Substitute T_ii = id in the left unit law at (i,i). The associator is then the identity on vertices. Its shift equation says s_n followed by s_n equals s_n, where s_n is the specified diagonal shift comparison. Cancel the invertible s_n to conclude s_n = id. Thus eqToIso(unit) commutes with the specified shift and the canonical identity shift. Lift it by Functor.mapTriangleIso and follow by Functor.mapTriangleIdIso. Its three components are precisely eqToIso(unit) on the vertices. The diagonal truncation equations identify its value on each truncation triangle with the stated composite.

proof.text: Choose the single-functor comparisons for each transition using the proved single-functor theorem. The cutoff equations are those already proved there. For the system triangle composition equation, the first and third components are the system truncation equations and the middle is the associator. Functor.mapTriangleCompIso has identity components, so componentwise extensionality proves the equality of triangle morphisms.

Steps: 1) the composition, naturality (η=a) and identity clauses of lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison give the system equation; types checked. 2) lem-pod-texact-truncation-triangle-comparison (m=r) gives the triple (c⁻,1,c⁺), its last square with the specified σ and naturality; composites are componentwise via step 1, and exactness of a is used. 3) Cutoff maps u, v come from the heart-lemma adjunctions (C≤r⊂C≤s; τ≥s+1K∈C≥r+1). The comparison squares were verified via ι_s and via T(π_r) = (c⁺)⁻¹π_{TK}. 4) TR3 on (u,1) gives w; the left adjunction forces w=v, so the cutoff triple is a triangle morphism. 5) The a1-cohomology-comparison-pasting q-formula is exactly h^r; naturality and composition (with composite shift comparisons, a exact) give the equation. For h_{i/i}=1, the unit associator's exactness forces σ=1, which is accepted. 6) Exact η: the third square follows from η's shift equation. Source: BBD 1.3.3(i),(ii) on printed pp. 29–30, plus 1.1.9/1.1.10 and 1.3.6, read; no SGA. Edge cases: trivial poset, zero category, r=s, out-of-range cutoffs, and K=A[−r] in D^b(Ab), which gives H^r=A in the heart with the [r] shift. Batch-5 flag: lem-pod-texact-truncation-triangle-comparison is an abstract t-structure lemma with generic stmt_deps and no proof_deps; it is not given by either assumption and is not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so the citation is accepted (same as Q93/Q76 for lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison). The four generic tool_uses are accepted. Advisory: a1-pasting's last sentence and lem-a1-texact-coefficient-stage-descent overlap the item's system clauses (pre-existing, not a delivery fault).
